card:
Goal: measure whether THIS Mac can reach the private repo shivinate7/session-mailbox with no prompt, and push one test message. Plan step 2 of decision session-messages. Read-only except one test message. Report each result in chat with exact exit codes and the first lines of any error. Never print a token or password. Never change settings.json, git config or stored credentials without asking the owner. If a command asks for a login, stop and tell the owner; do not type credentials.

1. Which computer: OS, lower-case hostname, and the GitHub account git uses (name only):
   uname -s; hostname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'; gh auth status 2>&1 | head -8   (if gh is missing, say "unknown")
2. Tools exist: ls -l ~/.claude/bin/mail   (if missing, stop and say so; the claude-settings SessionStart hook installs it)
3. Login check, no prompt:
   time GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git ls-remote https://github.com/shivinate7/session-mailbox.git refs/heads/mail; echo "exit $?"
   Report exit code, time, and whether it printed a ref line (40-hex hash + refs/heads/mail) or the exact error ("Authentication failed", "not found", a hang past 15 s). "not found" on a private repo means this Mac's account has no access.
4. Only if step 3 printed a ref line, send one test message:
   printf 'login test from %s Mac %s\n' "$(hostname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" "$(TZ=America/Chicago date '+%H:%M %Z')" | MAILBOX_REPO=https://github.com/shivinate7/session-mailbox.git ~/.claude/bin/mail send --to cloud/session_013NEJL1YBVqsXRPBac7nRcz --kind inform --body-file -; echo "exit $?"
   Report the output ("sent <id> to <addr>") and exit code. MAILBOX_REPO is set for this one command only.
4b. Prove the file landed (use the <id> from step 4):
   git --git-dir ~/.claude/mail.git ls-tree -r --name-only refs/heads/mail | grep '<id>'
   Report the line it prints, or "no file" if it prints nothing.
5. If step 3 failed, skip 4 and 4b. Report the exact failure and which fits: no GitHub login on this Mac; the account has no access to the repo; the login needs a prompt.

Also report whether the hostname from step 1 looks like the computer name the Claude app shows for this Mac. Done = one report from this Mac with steps 1 to 5 answered.
context:
Goal: measure whether your Mac and your Windows PC can both use the session mailbox.
Why yours: the card must run on your Mac, and no cloud session can reach it (measured 2026-11-10, list_computer_folders at 09:22 CST returned no folders).
Steps: open a new claude-settings session on your Mac. Copy the card text below and paste it in as your message. Paste what the session prints for steps 1 to 5, in particular the mail send line and the step 4b line, into the reply here. Then press Done.
Known: Windows (ssem-dpromax16) logged in, but mail send printed "sent" with no file stored; PR #2552 fixes it, not merged yet. So on the Mac "sent" alone proves nothing; step 4b shows whether the file landed. The login line is the part to read.
Meanwhile: the topic session waits and starts nothing.
home: step session-mailbox-followups; decision session-messages plan step 2
reply: Your question at 11:22 CST: why do you still have to run this by hand, when it was meant to be mechanical? The mechanical route is the git session mailbox (#2484, merged in batch 71): a cloud session leaves the test in the mailbox, and a session on your Mac picks it up and runs it with no step from you. Two things stop that today. (1) Nothing on your Mac reads the mailbox yet. This card is the first Mac run that proves it can, which is plan step 2, so it can't be sent through the mailbox. (2) The mailbox loses messages: your PC run said "sent" but stored no file. The fix runs in the messaging topic session (step mail-send-no-file). The other route, a Mac folder shared through Remote Control, also finds nothing: list_computer_folders returned no folders at 11:24 CST. After this one Mac run and that fix, later Mac tests go through the mailbox with no card. (Triage, 11:25 CST.)
title: Run the mailbox test card on your Mac
why: Plan step 2 of the mailbox needs one measure on each of your computers, and Windows is done.
